mainTopic: Whether a young goat can give birth within its first year, and what the disagreement between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון about the kid in the ברייתא is really about
overview: The גמרא first asks whether the ברייתא shows that an animal that expelled a murky discharge (מטנפת) cannot give birth again within its year. It rejects that idea, because the ברייתא is talking about an animal that really gave birth. Next it quotes רבי שמעון, who said he saw a kid whose offspring became subject to מעשר within its first year. The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between him and the תנא קמא. It offers four possible answers, and each one accepts the point the previous answer said they argued about. First, they argue about זעירי's rule that a discharge stops pregnancy for 30 days. Second, they argue about whether an animal can give birth after incomplete months, meaning early. Third, they argue about whether part of a day counts as a whole day (מקצת היום ככולו). Fourth, they argue about whether a מחוסר זמן animal, one still too young to be offered, enters the pen to be tithed.

steps.title: Does the תנא hold a discharging animal can't give birth again that year?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא's author holds a מטנפת cannot recover and give birth again within its year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the תנא holds that an animal that expels a murky discharge does not return and give birth within its year?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a possible inference about what the author of the ברייתא believes about a מטנפת, an animal that expelled a murky discharge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לימא means 'shall we say'. It signals a tentative suggestion that the גמרא is about to test. The idea is that the ברייתא's careful time limits only make sense if a מטנפת cannot give birth again within the same year.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion that the גמרא will test.
He holds, or he is of the opinion
An animal that expels a murky discharge instead of a normal birth
Within its year, meaning within the first year of its life

phrases.english: Shall we say he holds:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the author of the ברייתא the גמרא has just been discussing.

phrases.english: an animal that expels a murky discharge does not return
and give birth within its year?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא discussed just before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ברייתא's author hold that a מטנפת cannot give birth again within its year?

steps.title: No proof: a mother that actually gave birth is different
steps.stepSummary: The inference is rejected. Even if a מטנפת can give birth again within its year, an animal that actually gave birth surely cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say that a discharging animal returns and gives birth within its year, an animal that truly gave birth certainly does not return and give birth within its year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from Step 1. The ברייתא can be explained without that assumption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's case is about an animal that really gave birth, not one that just had a discharge. A real birth is much more draining, so everyone can agree that it cannot happen again within the same year. Because of that, the ברייתא tells us nothing about a מטנפת.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say. It brings in a 'what if' to show the proof does not work.
Certainly
Returns to fertility and gives birth again

phrases.english: If you say:
a discharging animal returns and gives birth
within its year —
one that actually gave birth certainly does not return
and give birth within its year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference proposed in Step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole inference about a מטנפת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא deals with a real birth, which is more limiting than a discharge, so it proves nothing about a מטנפת.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves nothing about a מטנפת. Its case is a real birth, and everyone can agree that a real birth cannot happen again within the same year.

steps.title: What is the difference between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's claim that he saw such a kid, then asks how his view differs from the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'I saw a kid', and so on. What is the difference between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's line from the ברייתא and asks what practical difference there is between him and the first opinion. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said he saw a kid whose offspring became subject to מעשר בהמה within its own first year. The תנא קמא seems to say something similar without that 'within its year' detail. The גמרא wants to know exactly where they would rule differently.

keyTerms.meaning: A young female goat (a kid)
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
What is the difference between...?

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
I saw a kid, etc.
phrases.notes: כו׳ means 'and so on'. The rest is his claim that the kid's offspring became subject to מעשר within its first year.

phrases.english: What is there between the first Tanna
and Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִיכָּא בֵּין תַּנָּא קַמָּא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the ברייתא and opens a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון

steps.title: First answer: they argue about זעירי's 30-day rule
steps.stepSummary: The difference between them is זעירי's rule. The תנא קמא accepts it and רבי שמעון does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is the statement of זעירי. The תנא קמא accepts זעירי's statement, and רבי שמעון does not accept it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. The two opinions split over whether to accept זעירי's earlier rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי taught that a discharge which counts legally is one that keeps the animal from getting pregnant for at least 30 days. Picture a goat that discharges at the start of its seventh month. If you follow זעירי, it cannot give birth until the second year, which is the view of the תנא קמא. Without זעירי, it could give birth within the first year, which is רבי שמעון's view.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
He accepts it / he does not accept it

phrases.english: There is between them the statement of Ze'eiri.
phrases.notes: This is זעירי's earlier rule that a discharge keeps the animal from getting pregnant for at least 30 days.

phrases.english: The first Tanna accepts the statement of Ze'eiri,
and Rabbi Shimon does not accept the statement of Ze'eiri.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether to accept זעירי's 30-day rule.

steps.title: Second answer: can an animal give birth early?
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, both accept זעירי. They argue whether an animal can give birth after incomplete months.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say that everyone accepts זעירי, and here they argue about whether an animal can give birth after incomplete months. The תנא קמא says it cannot, and רבי שמעון says it can.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to explain the argument, in which both opinions accept זעירי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both opinions accept the 30-day delay, then a normal pregnancy would push the birth into the second year. רבי שמעון says the animal can give birth a little early, so the birth still lands inside the first year. The תנא קמא says it cannot give birth early.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say. It introduces another possible answer.
Everyone agrees
Gives birth after incomplete months, meaning prematurely
They disagree

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
everyone accepts the statement of Ze'eiri,
and here they disagree about giving birth after incomplete months.
phrases.notes: 'Incomplete months' means the birth comes a bit before the pregnancy's full time is over.

phrases.english: According to the first Tanna, it does not give birth after incomplete months;
according to Rabbi Shimon, it does give birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דִּזְעֵירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to Step 3, in which both sides accept זעירי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about whether an animal can give birth after incomplete months.

steps.title: Third answer: does part of a day count as a whole day?
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, everyone agrees an animal does not give birth early. They argue about מקצת היום ככולו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say that everyone agrees an animal does not give birth after incomplete months, and here they argue about whether part of a day counts as the whole day. The תנא קמא says we do not say that, and רבי שמעון says we do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third possible answer. Both sides accept זעירי and both agree there is no early birth, so the argument is only about counting days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If part of a day counts as a full day, then the pregnancy can be finished on the very last day of the first year. That is רבי שמעון's view. The תנא קמא does not count part of a day as a whole day, so the earliest birth falls on the first day of the second year.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of the day counts like the whole day
We say it / we do not say it

phrases.english: And if you wish, say,
everyone agrees it does not give birth after incomplete months,
and here they disagree about whether part of the day is like all of it:
According to the first Tanna —
we do not say part of the day is like all of it;
according to Rabbi Shimon —
we do say part of the day is like all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אֵינָהּ יוֹלֶדֶת לִמְקוּטָּעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third answer to Step 3, agreeing on the points argued in Steps 4 and 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about whether part of a day counts as a whole day.
steps.whatToRemember: So far there are three possible explanations for the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון: (1) זעירי's 30-day rule, (2) whether an animal can give birth early, and (3) מקצת היום ככולו. Each new answer agrees with the earlier point and moves the argument to a smaller detail. The next step adds a fourth explanation.
steps.confusionAlert: The three answers are not three separate arguments that both sides hold at once. Each one is a separate, complete explanation of the same single disagreement, and each later answer accepts that both sides agree on what the earlier answer said they argued about.

steps.title: They argue whether a too-young animal enters the pen for tithing
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: everyone agrees that מקצת היום ככולו. The argument is whether a מחוסר זמן animal enters the pen to be tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say this instead: everyone agrees that part of a day counts like a whole day. Here they are arguing about whether an animal that is still too young to be offered can enter the pen to be tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more possible answer to the question from Step 3: what is the difference between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6 the argument was about מקצת היום ככולו. Now the גמרא says both sides accept that rule, so the argument must be about something else. It is whether a מחוסר זמן animal, one too young to be brought on the מזבח, enters the pen for מעשר. The תנא קמא says it does not enter, and רבי שמעון says it does.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'lacking time': an animal still too young to be brought as a קרבן
The pen where animals are gathered to be counted for tithing
To be tithed, meaning counted for מעשר בהמה, where every tenth animal is set apart

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא has now offered four ways to explain the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון: (1) זעירי's 30-day rule, (2) whether an animal can give birth after incomplete months, (3) מקצת היום ככולו, and (4) whether a מחוסר זמן animal enters the pen for tithing. Each new answer accepts the point the previous answer said they argued about, and moves the argument to a new detail.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with Step 6. There, מקצת היום ככולו was the point of the argument. Here everyone agrees to it, and the argument moves to a completely different question.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
that everyone agrees we say
part of the day is like the whole day,
and here, about an animal whose time has not yet come,
phrases.notes: He means an animal still too young to be offered on the מזבח.

phrases.english: whether it enters the pen to be tithed, they disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אָמְרִינַן מִקְצָת הַיּוֹם כְּכוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the rule that Step 6 treated as the point of the argument, and moves the disagreement to a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the practical difference between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether a מחוסר זמן animal enters the pen for מעשר. The תנא קמא says it does not, and רבי שמעון says it does.
